title: StreamLayer Orchestrator: hierarchical tool chaining, result weaving, and recursion sentinels
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a StreamLayer Orchestrator that supports hierarchical multi-tool chaining with token-level streaming of partial tool outputs, deterministic result weaving into conversational context, and a configurable set of recursion/loop sentinels to prevent runaway tool cycles. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, telemetry, and gradual rollout with a compatibility shim for legacy function-call contracts.
background: Current executor supports linear tool chains but struggles with: (1) streaming partial outputs from tools back to the API user while other tools are still executing, (2) consistent deterministic injection of tool results into structured outputs without corrupting the chat state, and (3) robust detection of recursion/loops when tools invoke other tools (or the same) via function calling. Past work focused on halting policies and simple cycle counters but didn't support hierarchical nesting or incremental streaming semantics.
proposal: Introduce StreamLayer Orchestrator as a thin execution layer between the runtime invoker and tool adapters. Key behaviors: (a) hierarchical chaining graph where nodes are tools or model calls and edges carry a streaming contract, (b) result weaving algorithm that incrementally merges partial tool outputs into a structured output envelope while preserving provenance metadata, (c) recursion sentinels: depth threshold, per-request cycle fingerprinting, and time-to-live (TTL) for active tool frames, and (d) compatibility shim that accepts older function-call shapes and maps them to the new structured envelope.
acceptance_criteria: Token-level streaming: client receives partial tool outputs as they are emitted and sees a final merged structured response identical to non-streamed execution
Deterministic weaving: merging two interleaved tool outputs yields reproducible structured state under same inputs and ordering
Loop protection: requests that exceed configured depth (default 6) or hit a repeated call fingerprint are gracefully stopped and return a controlled fallback rather than hanging
Compatibility shim: legacy function-call requests are accepted and translated with no visible regressions for existing customers
Telemetry: events for tool_enter/tool_exit/partial_stream/merge_conflict/loop_sentinel fire and are viewable in Console dashboards
Automated unit and integration tests covering nested chains, partial streaming, merge heuristics, and sentinel triggers

risks: Merging partial structured outputs can produce conflicts when two tools write overlapping keys; we need a deterministic conflict resolution policy
Streaming increases surface area for deadlocks if backpressure isn't propagated correctly through adapters
Compatibility shim could introduce subtle behavioral differences for malformed legacy calls
Telemetry volume for token-level events may be high; need sampling strategies
decisions: Use deterministic last-writer-wins merge with explicit provenance array for conflicted fields
Default recursion depth set to 6, configurable per-customer and per-route
Fingerprint cycle detection by hashing (tool_id, input_signature, parent_frame_id) and store in request-scoped set
Expose soft-fallback policy: when sentinel triggers, optionally invoke a fallback model variant or return partial structured response with 'incomplete': true flag
